A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Rewind-to-Delete work. All 30 pages, including Appendices A–E, are available and readable; text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v6 reports original eICU and Lacuna-100 experiments, membership attacks, timing and checkpoint-reconstruction measurements, and an LLM unlearning experiment in Appendix B.

after.justification: v7 retains these original experimental results, including the main comparisons and supplementary experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same training, checkpoint reconstruction, rewinding, retained-data gradient updates, and Gaussian perturbation procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate eICU length-of-stay prediction, Lacuna-100 gender classification with user-level unlearning, and Alpaca math-task unlearning with Mistral-7B in Appendix B.4.

E2.justification: Hessian-Free, Constrained Newton Step, Finetune, Fisher Forgetting, SCRUB, and retraining retain their participation in the corresponding comparisons. The LLM retraining and finetuning comparators are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain the same data selection, model configurations, batch sizes, training budgets, noise settings, and AUC, membership-attack, and BLEU evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The rewind-percentage and noise analyses, checkpoint-reconstruction experiments, membership-attack analyses, and t-SNE visualizations are retained without changes to their evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains five-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times, 100 undersampling repetitions for classic MIA, the same seed/noise-reuse disclosures, and one-sigma uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 2–3 and 6–15 are unchanged, including AUC, membership-attack, BLEU, timing, and reconstruction measurements. The plotted results also match.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, Equation (4), gains an additive O(σ²) term, and Appendix A.2 replaces the corresponding perturbation calculation and adds σ² to its final inequality. This materially weakens the reported nonconvex utility guarantee: at fixed noise, the bound retains a noise-dependent residual when its other terms shrink. The privacy guarantee and PL corollaries are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about first-order black-box certified unlearning, PL generalization guarantees, and empirical advantages.

C2.justification: The interpretations and Appendix C limitations are unchanged. In particular, the convergence discussion following Equation (4) is retained without a new qualification addressing the added σ² term.

D1.justification: The implementation, preprocessing, hyperparameter, hardware, and code/data-access disclosures are unchanged. The only changed external hyperlink is the paper's own arXiv version link.

R1.justification: Section 1.1, Appendix E, and the bibliography are unchanged, with the same cited works and research positioning.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date header is updated, and the brief lead-in to the revised proof calculation changes its stated expansion target. The narrative and section order are otherwise preserved.

P2.justification: Equation (4) occupies additional lines, causing local reflow across pages 6–10; the shortened proof also changes spacing on page 18. All figures and tables retain their content and structure, with limited positioning changes.

improvement.justification: v7 explicitly includes a noise contribution in Equation (4), but Appendix A.2's replacement derivation equates the same squared-gradient quantity with itself plus σ². v6's corresponding calculation also unjustifiably substituted parameter noise for a gradient difference. The attempted theoretical repair therefore remains unsupported by a valid displayed derivation, while the empirical evidence is unchanged. These effects leave the net quality direction uncertain.
